notes: Both coders found the same two NIU university-layer pages (teaching guidance, student page) and both set stance delegates with the same three tiers. Main disagreements: (1) phase and actor on borderline items, such as support services (general vs before-course), the 'faculty may require' bullets (instructor/course-start vs student/during-work) and ask-your-professor items; resolved by re-reading the sentence and applying one rule across sibling units. (2) modality on list items under 'be especially careful' (should-not) and 'you should always' (should) rather than must-not/must. (3) policy_type on three units: description of how AI was used coded P24 not P25; the cite-real-authors item and 'use beyond these purposes' made UNCOVERED rather than stretched into P31/P24/P01; in-class/oral assessment kept P33 with both fit notes. (4) unit_stance (e.g. limited-use tier is restrict, rationale sentences neutral). (5) One coder's policy was null on fragmentary anchors; the other's normalized policy was checked against the source and used. Single-coder units: heading-only units (Option 1 heading, Sample Frameworks heading) and two product-description lines (Adobe, Quinncia) were dropped; the rest were real statements and kept. Matching was by source passage; where one coder merged two clauses of a sentence the clauses were kept as separate units and counted as unmatched.
